item_name: SiamMOT (Shuai et al., CVPR 2021) - code-level re-check of the explicit motion model, visibility head, training labels and how the predicted box enters association
depth_level: Full analysis with official code. The relevant training, loss, sampling, inference and solver source files of amazon-science/siam-mot (branch main) were read line by line. The paper (arXiv v1 HTML) was re-checked for the equations, the triplet ablation, Table 7, Table 11 and the appendices. The earlier paper-level review (research_flyvis_next_change_2026-10-23/results/N10_SiamMOT_TrackTrack_MOTIP.json) is not repeated except where the code contradicts or sharpens it.
bibliography: (1) Bing Shuai, Andrew Berneshawi, Xinyu Li, Davide Modolo, Joseph Tighe (Amazon Web Services). SiamMOT: Siamese Multi-Object Tracking. CVPR 2021. arXiv:2105.11595 (v1, 25 May 2021), HTML https://arxiv.org/html/2105.11595v1 , PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.11595 . CVF open-access proceedings version (pages 12372-12382 [uncertain], not opened in this session). The arXiv v1 and CVPR versions are one study, not two confirmations. SiamMOT+ (the TAO-person variant with an added re-ID linking step, paper Table 5) is the same system plus one module and does not confirm anything independently. full_text_checked: Code: every file listed in bibliography was printed raw from raw.githubusercontent.com (stdout only, nothing executed or saved). video_augmentation.py was read only to line 150, so the image crop-resize motion simulator (image_augmentation.py) was not opened. Not opened: eval code, IMM implementation (it is absent from the public repository: only the EMM model and sampler are registered in the tree), demos, model_zoo.md, train/test entry points. Paper: arXiv v1 HTML re-read through a fetch tool that summarises pages. I asked it for Eq. 4-6, Section 3.2-3.4, Section 5.1-5.3, Table 2, Table 7, Table 11 and Appendices A, B and G. Table 1-3 numbers match the earlier PDF-based review N10. The Table 7 and Table 11 numbers come only from that fetch tool and were not checked against the PDF [uncertain]. No supplementary material outside arXiv was accessed.
inputs_state_output: Authors' setup (verified in code): one jointly trained Faster R-CNN (DLA-34 + FPN, 128 channels) gives detections and the features for tracking. Per active track, the state (TrackPool cache) holds three things: (a) a template feature map, ROIAlign 15x15x128 (POOLER_RESOLUTION 15) cut from the FPN level chosen by box size, re-extracted EVERY frame from the track's latest output box; (b) a search region, the same box enlarged to 2x width and height (SEARCH_REGION 2.0 gives expansion 1.0; extend_bbox) in padded image coordinates (PAD_PIXELS 512); (c) the last box. On the next frame the search region is pooled to 30x30x128. A depthwise cross-correlation (xcorr_depthwise: each channel of the template slides over the same channel of the search map) gives a 16x16x128 response. Two 3x3 conv+GN+ReLU towers then produce per-location 2-class visibility logits, a centerness logit and 4 ReLU box offsets (l,t,r,b). At inference these maps are bicubically upsampled x16. The output box comes from the offsets at argmax_xy[(softmax_vis * sigmoid(centerness) * scale_penalty) * (1 - lambda) + lambda * Hann window], lambda = COSINE_WINDOW_WEIGHT 0.4. So the window is ADDED, not multiplied as in paper Eq. 4-5, and the scale penalty is exp(0.1 * (1 - s_w * s_h)), not the Gaussian the paper describes. The returned confidence is the raw visibility softmax at that location, without centerness or penalties. Dormant (suspended) tracks keep the cache from their last active frame. Each frame they are searched again in the SAME fixed 2x region around the last seen box, with the same template, for up to MAX_DORMANT_FRAMES = 30 frames (both public configs); there is no motion extrapolation. Assignment context: none is learned. Ours: bounded grey crop (eye) rendered into 721 hexagonal columns. FlyVis recurrent state runs over the exemplar frames and then the search frames. A ridge target model is fitted on 4 exemplar frames, so the template is fixed per query rather than refreshed every frame. The readout gets 68 regional activity features pooled per real detection region, an observed-target descriptor, 8 geometry inputs and 6 assignment-context features, and gives one scalar score per candidate action. Key structural difference: SiamMOT keeps the template-vs-search relation resolved at every offset (a 16x16 grid with 128 channels before the towers), and the box is regressed from that map. Our readout sees the activity map only after pooling inside each detector region (68 numbers). Relations between the template pattern and each offset, and layout inside the region, are not available to the head, and the box is copied from the detector. The project's ridge response over 721 columns (the 'D map', e.g. observed_response_maps.npz holds 721-long vectors) is a dense map, but only for a linear filter fitted online on 4 frames. Downstream it has been read as 3 peaks or as pooled region features, never through a learned dense correlation head.
action_and_refusal: Verified in roi_heads.py, box_head/inference.py and track_solver.py: (1) Tracking branch: the EMM box of every active and dormant track is passed back through the detector box head as a proposal (_refine_tracks). The box is REPLACED by the box-head regression of the EMM box. The score becomes 1 + (p_person from the box head + EMM visibility) / 2: the box head adds +1 to track probabilities so tracks skip its score threshold and NMS, and _refine_tracks adds +1 to the EMM score. With TRACKTOR=False, the visibility tested against the threshold is therefore the MEAN of detector appearance probability and Siamese visibility, not v_i alone as paper Eq. 4 and Section 3.4 say. The paper does not mention this box-head refinement. (2) Solver: tracks and detections are concatenated. Active tracks get another +1, so scores fall in [2,3] for active tracks, [1,2] for dormant tracks and [0,1) for detections. One class-agnostic NMS at IoU 0.5 then runs. Consequence: when a Siamese box conflicts with a detection (IoU > 0.5), the track box ALWAYS wins, whatever its confidence, and the detection is deleted. Detections never correct or replace a track box. Their only role is to start new tracks (score >= START_TRACK_THRESH 0.6) where no track box overlaps them. A dormant track's box also suppresses overlapping detections. The dormant track resumes its old ID if its mean score is >= RESUME_TRACK_THRESH 0.4. An active track whose mean score is < TRACK_THRESH 0.4 is suspended and its ID is set to -1 for that frame. An active track removed by NMS under another active track is also suspended. A weak track box can therefore block a detection from starting a new track in that frame. (3) Abstention: there is no 'keep the default' choice, because the Siamese box IS the default path. The only refusal is the visibility gate (continue vs make dormant), together with resume vs stay dormant and expiry after 30 frames. No learned estimate of whether the Siamese box is better than the alternative detection exists. Ours: a selected real detection box is transferred into the track state before native ByteTrack matching, as an optional override of a well-performing default assignment, with a fixed no-action logit 0. SiamMOT therefore gives NO precedent for a learned advantage-over-default gate. Its conflict rule is a fixed priority (track over detection), justified by the tracker being the main localiser.
labels_and_loss: Verified in target_sampler.py and track_loss.py; several points differ from the paper text. Pair formation: two frames from a 1 s window of a video (VideoDataset, TEMPORAL_WINDOW 1000 ms, 2 random frames, kept in order), or two augmented copies of one image (ImageDataset, frames_per_image 2; motion is simulated on one copy by crop-resize with MOTION_LIMIT 0.05-0.1, plus motion blur, JPEG compression, colour jitter on one copy, and a shared flip). Proposals: RPN proposals of frame t get an identity by IoU. FG_IOU_THRESHOLD 0.65 gives id = gt id, BG_IOU_THRESHOLD 0.35 gives id = -1 (background), and IoU in between gives -2 (ignored). Per image the budget is PROPOSAL_PER_IMAGE 256 samples, at most POS_RATIO 0.25 * 256 = 64 positives and HN_RATIO 0.25 * 256 = 64 hard negatives; easy negatives fill the rest. Positive: template = a proposal of the same identity (a jittered box, IoU >= 0.65); search region = that proposal enlarged 2x, pooled from the OTHER frame (feature batch odd/even swap); target = that identity's ground-truth box in the other frame. If the identity is missing in the other frame, the target is a dummy box [-1,-1,-1,-1] and every location is negative. Hard negative (code meaning): template = the exact gt box of identity i; search region = a proposal of ANOTHER identity j with height ratio in [0.5, 2], enlarged 2x; target = identity i's box in the other frame. Most locations are labelled negative, but if i itself lies in the distractor-centred window, its true location is positive. The model is thus taught to find the real target and reject a similar-scale neighbour placed at the window centre. At most one sample per distinct other identity is drawn. Easy negative: template = background proposal (id -1, objectness >= 0.3, width and height >= 5 px); dummy target, all locations negative. Dense labels: a location is positive only inside the CENTRAL part of the target box. Location x must be more than 0.8 * half-width from both vertical edges (CLS_POS_REGION 0.8), which is the central 20% x 20% of the box, about 4% of its area. The paper says positives are anywhere inside the box. Losses: visibility = 2-class log-softmax NLL averaged SEPARATELY over positive and negative locations and combined 0.5/0.5 (SiamRPN-style class balancing), NOT the focal loss stated in paper Eq. 6. Box = FCOS-style -log((I+1)/(U+1)) IoU loss on positive locations, weighted by the centerness target sqrt(min(l,r)/max(l,r) * min(t,b)/max(t,b)). Centerness = BCE on positive locations. All three are scaled by TRACK_LOSS_WEIGHT 1.0 (0.1 in the AOT config) and added to the RPN and detection losses for joint end-to-end training. The labels are therefore pure localisation/identity labels taken from ground-truth boxes. They are not the consequence of any assignment, and they are dense: every positive sample supplies dozens of positive locations and hundreds of negatives. Imbalance is handled by the 0.5/0.5 class averaging and the fixed 64/64/rest sample mix. No neutral class exists, and no event is rare by construction.
data_camera_resolution_rate: Training (configs and Section 4.2/5): ablation models are trained on images only. For MOT17 and CRP this means CrowdHuman full-box (crowdhuman_train_fbox + val_fbox, 25k iterations, DLA_34_FPN_EMM_MOT17.yaml); the general config uses COCO17 + CrowdHuman visible-box with 50k iterations. 16 pairs per batch on 8 GPUs, SGD with LR 0.02 and steps at 60%/80% of training, weight decay 1e-4. Train scales are 640-960 on the shorter side (max 1280-1500); test uses shorter side 800. The MOT17 config sets AMODAL True and USE_GIVEN_DETECTIONS True (public detections re-scored and regressed by the box head). Evaluation: MOT17-train (7 videos, 14-30 fps, mix of static and moving cameras), Caltech Roadside Pedestrians (CRP, 7 long car-mounted videos, strong camera motion, not exhaustively annotated), TAO-person val (826 videos, includes BDD clips), MOT17-test and HiEve test. Video training pairs are at most 1 s apart. Initial condition: a track starts from a detection with score >= 0.6 and its template is that detection's feature. Unlike our 4-frame ridge fit, there is no multi-frame exemplar. Nothing was run on BDD100K MOT, on grey low-light input, or with a bounded biological front-end.

distinguishing_ablations: (a) Explicit vs implicit motion (Table 1). The difference is a whole head, not one factor. IMM concatenates the two search-region feature maps into a 2-layer MLP (512 hidden) that regresses one motion vector. EMM uses depthwise correlation, conv towers and dense per-location visibility and box supervision. Gain: +1.8 MOTA and +0.9 IDF1 on MOT17-train (7 videos), +0.6 TAP on TAO, and nothing on CRP (76.4 vs 76.8 MOTA). EMM is better on 2 of 3 datasets, with single runs, no seeds and no intervals. The authors credit 'explicit template matching'. Section 3.3 also says pixel-level supervision reduces false matches to distractors, but no ablation separates correlation from dense supervision. The IMM code is not in the public repository, so its exact inputs could not be checked. (b) Training triplets (Table 2 and Table 7). Removing N (P+H) leaves false-positive tracks alive: MOT17 FP 9639 vs 5726, MOTA 59.7 vs 63.3. Removing H (P+N) increases ID switches: MOT17 697 vs 671, CRP 1758 vs 1311 [Table 7 uncertain], and lowers CRP IDF1 79.0 vs 81.1. So distractor-centred hard samples mainly protect identity and true-negative samples mainly protect track termination. Note that the code's 'hard' sample is a window centred on another identity of similar scale, which is more specific than the paper's definition ('search region does not contain the target'). (c) Joint training: 63.3 vs 61.5 MOTA. The backbone features matter, not only the head. (d) tau (Table 3): IDF1 rises from 58.4 to 60.8 at tau = 15 and saturates by about 30 frames, because people leave the fixed 2x search region of a dormant track. On CRP, tau > 1 has no effect. (e) Thresholds (Table 11): the continuation and birth thresholds trade FP against FN and ID switches roughly monotonically. There is no free gain. (f) Not ablated anywhere: box-head refinement of track boxes, averaging detector and Siamese scores, track-over-detection NMS priority, the centre-region positive ratio, and the code-paper discrepancies in loss (balanced CE vs focal) and in decoding. All ablations are single runs.
explanations_addressed: Lost discriminative/spatial information in the readout: DESIGN ANALOGY, moderate. EMM's advantage over IMM is the closest evidence that keeping the template-vs-search relation at every offset, with per-location supervision, beats feeding features to an MLP that regresses one output. The effect is small (+1.8 MOTA), absent on fast camera motion (CRP), and confounded (correlation, conv towers and dense labels change together; IMM has about 400x more parameters). It suggests, but does not prove, that our region-pooled 68 features are the bottleneck; our own z13_region_pooling_v1 (mean vs max pooling) was negative, so the pooling operator alone is not the answer. Target-vs-neighbour identification: DIRECT DESIGN PRECEDENT. Hard samples whose search window is centred on another same-scale identity, with the true target positive only where it really is, lower ID switches (Table 2 and Table 7). The project's comparable signal is the rank of the correct region against the baseline-assigned neighbour. Training objective mismatched to final assignment: CAUTION. SiamMOT never trains on assignment consequences. It trains pure localisation, and the solver gives the tracker box absolute priority. It works because the Siamese box is the main localiser for every track at every frame, not a rare override. This argues that dense localisation targets are learnable, but SiamMOT gives no method for estimating the advantage over a strong default. Rare useful events with high harm cost: NOT ADDRESSED. There is no selective override; the harm of a wrong Siamese box is controlled only by the visibility threshold (Table 11 trade-off) and the box-head re-scoring. Insufficient history: PARTLY. The template is only the last frame (refreshed every frame), and the dormant-track search is fixed at the last location. Gains saturate at about 30 frames because objects leave the search window. Longer memory was left to future work and SiamMOT+ re-ID. Limits of the action: DIRECT ANALOGY. The Siamese box is confined to the 2x search window, just as our action is confined to the eye. The window prior (lambda) had to be lowered to 0.1 for fast motion, and objects outside the window (the analogue of our 334 cases with the correct detection outside the eye) cannot be recovered by this mechanism at all.
evidence_strength: Peer-reviewed (CVPR 2021). Official code is public and was read in this session for the training, loss, sampler, decoding and solver paths. The IMM baseline code is not released. The paper's numbers are single runs on few videos (MOT17-train 7, CRP 7), with no seeds or confidence intervals. The EMM vs IMM gap is small and inconsistent across datasets. The code differs from the paper text in four places: balanced CE vs focal loss, central 20% positive region vs whole box, additive vs multiplicative window, and a mean of detector and Siamese scores vs pure visibility at the threshold. The appendix also has a contradictory alpha/beta naming. SiamMOT is widely used as a baseline, but no independent replication of its ablations was located (not searched exhaustively). Overall: MODERATE as an engineering design reference; WEAK as causal evidence that a dense correlation readout would fix our specific failure (advantage estimation for rare overrides).
difference_from_tried: Compared with what the project already tried: (1) Fixed or learned association of 3 D peaks (KeepTrack-inspired): those used peaks of the ridge response map, a linear filter fitted on 4 exemplars. SiamMOT instead learns the matching function itself (depthwise correlation, then conv towers) across thousands of identities with distractor-centred hard samples. The project has never trained a matching function over the FlyVis activity map with dense location labels. z13_pairwise_map_v1 and z13_map_only104_v1 trained readouts of the map with BCE/rank losses on candidates, not per-location dense labels with a regressed box. (2) Ridge target model: same role as SiamMOT's template, but SiamMOT refreshes the template every frame from the output box, while ours is fixed on 4 exemplars and the FlyVis state drifts over search frames. (3) Per-action MSE to good-minus-harm with a softmax-threshold policy (z13_box_supervision_followup_v1): SiamMOT has no counterpart. Its labels are ground-truth target locations, not decision consequences, and its 'policy' is a fixed priority plus a visibility threshold. (4) Category replacement and full-box transfer (z13_box_proposal_v1): SiamMOT regresses its own box and then snaps it with the detector box head, instead of choosing among detector boxes. (5) Context features: SiamMOT uses none in the learned part; context enters only through the NMS/threshold rules. What is genuinely new for us: (a) a dense, offset-resolved template-vs-search correlation over the hex activity map; (b) supervising it with dense identity-aware location labels and distractor-centred hard samples instead of rare consequence labels; (c) per-frame template refresh. What is NOT new: negative samples (scripts/z13_train.py already has kind = 0 refusal samples), cosine-window or geometry priors, and the use of a dense map as such.
candidate_node_change: Node: FlyVis activity readout (plus target state), not the tracker. Change: replace the 'pool 68 features per detection region, then regress an action score' readout with a SiamMOT-style dense correlation readout on the hex lattice. Template T = the FlyVis output activity (34 cell types) on a small hex neighbourhood around the target in the last exemplar or confirmed frame. Search S = the activity over all 721 columns on the query frame. Response R = depthwise (per cell type) correlation of T over S on the hex grid, followed by two small hex-conv layers that give per-column visibility logits and per-column box offsets (l,t,r,b) in eye coordinates, plus a cosine prior centred on the tracker prediction. Training labels come from BDD100K ground truth, not decision outcomes: positives are the columns in the central part of the same identity's true box in the query frame; hard samples are eye windows centred on another identity of similar scale, with the target positive only where it really is; negatives are windows with no target. Use balanced 0.5/0.5 CE and centerness-weighted IoU. Action use: pick the real detection whose box best agrees with the decoded box (or whose centre carries the highest response). Keep 'no action' unless decoded visibility exceeds a threshold fitted on the fit20 videos only. Why it targets a FlyVis problem: it addresses the readout losing spatial and identity information (the activity map is collapsed into 68 pooled numbers per region) and the weak, rare training signal (13-33 outcome-changing actions selected out of 4183 fit20 rows). Equal controls, same head, same labels, same splits: old D readout (68 pooled features, existing heads); stock FlyVis C with the dense head; eye input R1 (raw grey hex input) with the dense head, the decisive control because dense correlation on raw pixels may do just as well; no-fly geometry (cosine prior + IoU to prediction only). Result of the fly only if D-dense > R1-dense and D-dense > C-dense. Cheap distinguishing check: in the inspected caches only pooled features exist (runs/z13_candidate_reserve_20261021/*/cache_*.npz holds features (n,3,68), centers and scores; parity audits hold 721-long response vectors), so a full-map check needs per-column 34-type activity maps [uncertain whether such maps are saved anywhere else]. If they are saved for train26: on CPU, train the dense head on the train84 videos (localisation labels only) and test on the 26 evaluation videos. Report (i) the rate at which the correct high-confidence detection outranks the baseline-assigned detection among the 553 wrong-assignment cases with the correct detection inside the eye, and (ii) the same rate on correctly assigned cases (harm proxy), with paired video bootstrap, for D/C/R1/geometry. Pre-register: proceed to GPU map generation and a HOTA pilot only if D-dense improves (i) by at least 10 pp over the old D pooled readout, beats R1-dense with a positive lower CI bound, and keeps (ii) within 1 pp of baseline. Otherwise record it as a negative readout-node result. If maps are not saved, the first stage is a bounded GPU regeneration for a subset of videos (see cost), with the 07:40 MSK deadline controller.
strongest_objection: SiamMOT solves a different problem. Its Siamese box is the PRIMARY localiser for every track on every frame, and detections are subordinate (deleted on conflict). Our failure is selecting a rare beneficial override of a strong default assignment and estimating its advantage. A better localiser does not by itself tell us when overriding helps, and SiamMOT offers no gate beyond a visibility threshold that trades FP against FN (Table 11). In addition, (1) the EMM vs IMM gain is small (+1.8 MOTA), single-run and absent on the fast-motion car-camera dataset closest to BDD100K conditions (CRP 76.4 vs 76.8). (2) Its matching power comes from a 128-channel jointly trained CNN on CrowdHuman/COCO, while FlyVis gives 34 grey cell-type maps with few parameters, so the R1 control may match or beat it. (3) Our own project data already show the readout of the map beats R1 strongly (z13_map_only104_v1 D_map-R1_map +14.2 pp) without turning into HOTA gains, so better identification may again not convert.
cost_and_hardware: CPU, saved features only: not possible for the dense head, because the inspected caches hold only 68-dim pooled features per region or peak. If per-column maps exist for train26/train84, a 721-column, 34-channel hex-correlation head (well under 50k parameters) trains on CPU in minutes to about an hour per seed [uncertain]. GPU: regenerating per-column FlyVis activity maps for exemplar and query frames needs new FlyVis forward passes on one 12 GB GPU. Map storage for about 37k queries at 721 x 34 float16 is roughly 1.8 GB per representation (D, C, R1) [uncertain estimate]; it is feasible in one bounded night run with the deadline controller, but must be costed with a price probe first, as in z13_full_box_supervision_v1.
